name: Emblem Tidewall
specific_features: Starship crash site (colony ship, warship, freighter)
Automated beacon (distress, navigation, or unknown purpose)
description: Emblem Tidewall is a massive oceanic world where a single chain of volcanic mountains breaches the surface like a wall dividing the global ocean into two distinct hemispheres. This mountain chain, rising over twelve kilometers above sea level in places, runs pole to pole and creates dramatically different ocean conditions on either side: calm, warm waters to the east and storm-wracked, cold currents to the west. A planet-spanning hurricane perpetually circulates the western ocean, feeding on the temperature differential.

The dense atmosphere amplifies every sound, turning the crash of waves against the Tidewall mountains into a thunder that never ceases. Marine fauna in the eastern calm have evolved elaborate bioluminescent displays for communication, turning entire bays into canvases of shifting light. The western ocean is darker, rougher, and home to larger, more aggressive species adapted to the eternal storm.

A colony ship of considerable size lies half-submerged against the Tidewall's eastern face, its hull breached and colonized by marine organisms over what appears to be centuries. The ship's automated distress beacon still pulses weakly, drawing the occasional salvage crew, but its passenger manifest and origin remain unidentified. Coral-like growths have incorporated the ship's hull plating into their structure, creating a hybrid reef of metal and biology that extends for kilometers.

The Tidewall's unique geography makes it a natural laboratory for studying divergent evolution in real time, with genetically related species developing dramatically different adaptations on either side. Titanium salvage from the colony ship remains commercially viable, but the reef ecosystem that has grown around it is scientifically irreplaceable. The distress beacon's signal occasionally shifts frequency in patterns that do not match any known automated protocol, suggesting either malfunction or something still operating within the wreck.
